overview: Black plays 2...Na6 against the Caro-Kann main set-up, heading for c7 to support ...e5 or ...d5. The main line goes 3.Nc3 Nc7 4.Nf3 d5 and Black reaches a Caro-Kann structure with an oddly placed knight. It is solid but passive and seldom played, and White can take space with an early e5.

white_ideas.idea: Take space with e5 or Bd3 and develop naturally
Exploit the placement of the Black knight

black_ideas.idea: Reroute the knight to c7 and play ...d5 or ...e5
Keep the solid Caro-Kann pawn structure

typical_structures.structure: Caro-Kann structure with Black c6 and d5 pawns

character.notes: Black keeps a compact Caro-Kann pawn structure with few weaknesses, and play is steady rather than forcing.

soundness.notes: Passive but playable; strong players do not consider it refuted.

structure.notes: The d5 and c6 pawns against e4 usually leave a semi-open centre.

approach.notes: A rare reply that strong players seldom use.

level.notes: Plans are clear enough but the knight route needs thought.

character.reason: The compact pawn structure and slow knight manoeuvre give a steady game that is hard to break down.

soundness.reason: It is a passive but sound setup.

structure.reason: Black c6 and d5 against e4 give half-open files in most lines.

level.reason: The set-up is simple but it needs judgement about the knight and e5.

plans.reason: There is no clear named plan.
